hypothesis: A buried normal fault separates a demagnetized fault-core thin sheet (magnetic structural index N_m ~ 1) from the displaced hanging-wall syntectonic wedge density contact (gravity structural index N_g ~ 0); the oriented doublet across +grad(depth_to_base) locates the subcrop trace up-dip of the gravity inflection.

amendments.reason: Concurrent merged review (research/session-f34477d2-review.md, PR #199) correctly states that Gaussian smoothing is not physical upward continuation (Fourier multipliers exp(-sigma^2|k|^2/2) vs exp(-|k|h)) and that a Gaussian scale-slope is not generally an Euler structural index. The originating session-c59db412 hypothesis text used that loose language; this preregistration must not inherit it.
amendments.corrected_operator: Structural index N is estimated only by windowed least-squares solution of the Euler homogeneity equation from spatial derivatives (dx, dy, dz) of gravity/magnetic grids. If continuation is used at all, it is physical FFT upward continuation with multiplier exp(-|k|h) at frozen heights. Gaussian blur scale-slopes are prohibited as an index estimator.
amendments.additional_frozen_gate: Before any holdout run, the estimator must pass a synthetic forward-model validation: recover known N and depth within preregistered tolerances for isolated synthetic sheet/contact/dike/sphere sources at multiple depths with realistic noise and interfering sources. Failure retires the lane as negative without consuming a holdout experiment.
